purpose: Publish more than one defensible PM rating while keeping every result tied to the same evidence judgments.

alternativeProfiles.definition: Prioritises broad material outcomes, durable reform, inclusion, productivity, poverty reduction, and crisis resilience. Physical infrastructure has a separate specialist rubric.
Prioritises poverty, health, education, broad access, and distribution alongside aggregate outcomes.
Prioritises institutions, liberties, integrity, accountability, and crisis restraint.

reviewPerspectives.mainFinding: Poverty, infrastructure, services, and productive capacity deserved more visible credit, while jobs quality and inclusion still limit the result.

Institutions and integrity must retain 25% combined weight, but the prior 3.8 institutions score was too severe without clearer calibration against the Emergency and surviving electoral and judicial checks.
The prior arithmetic was reproducible, but several stored PM headlines did not exactly match their components and demonetisation could explain only about 0.05-0.20 balanced points.

Operational security is a comparative strength, but prevention failures, the China border shock, Manipur, and safeguards require a lower rights-adjusted score and only a bounded increase in the balanced PM total.

publicationRules: Compute every headline directly from component scores and published weights.
Apply a formula change to every rated PM term, never one favoured leader.
Show the balanced result as the headline and publish all alternative lens results beside it.
Describe the lens range as priority sensitivity, not a confidence interval.
Treat policy ratings as evidence inputs, not automatic line-item additions or deductions.
Do not count the same policy failure independently in several components without distinct outcome evidence.
Keep observed change during a term separate from proof that the PM caused the change.

demonetisationSensitivity.note: This bounded effect is not an independently identified causal estimate; it prevents one policy from dominating or being counted repeatedly.
